chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from al-Khaybari, from Yunus ibn Zabyan and al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Two characteristics: whoever has them is good; otherwise, stay away from him, stay away from him, stay away from him. It was asked: 'What are they?' He said: 'Prayer at its times, and maintaining it, and mutual assistance (al-muwasah).'
ai.seo_question: What are the two characteristics that make a person good according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights that true virtue is anchored in the dual pillars of ritual fidelity—specifically praying at its precise appointed times (mawaqit)—and social solidarity, known as 'al-muwasah'. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis that spiritual correctness in worship must be complemented by active generosity and mutual aid within the community, serving as the definitive test of a believer's character.
